title: Chemical Reactions
seo_title: Grade 8 Natural Sciences: Chemical Reactions Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: In a chemical reaction, reactants change into new products; atoms are rearranged but not created or destroyed. Signs of a chemical reaction; word equations and simple balanced equations; conservation of mass. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 8, Matter and Materials: Chemical reactions)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): reactants and products, signs of a chemical reaction, word equations, balancing and conservation of mass. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed.
key_sub: The total mass stays the same.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a chemical reaction, the reactants change into new substances called products. Signs include a colour change, a gas (bubbles), a change in temperature, light or a precipitate. Burning, rusting and cooking are chemical reactions.

A word equation shows the change: magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide. Atoms are rearranged, so the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants (conservation of mass). Balanced equations have the same number of each kind of atom on both sides.

Example

Name the product: carbon + oxygen → ?

Carbon and oxygen join.

Answer: carbon dioxide

Example

12 g of magnesium reacts with 8 g of oxygen. What is the mass of magnesium oxide?

Mass is conserved.

Answer: 20 g

Common mistakes

  • Thinking mass is lost when a gas escapes.
  • Thinking melting is a chemical reaction.
  • Changing the small numbers in formulas to balance.

items.q:
Mass
vinegar26 g
bicarbonate of soda38 g
total after reaction64 g
Aisha mixed vinegar and bicarbonate of soda inside a sealed bag. Gas formed. What does the data show?
c: Mass was conserved because no matter could escape.
Mass was created by the reaction.
Mass was lost because a gas formed.
items.e: 26 + 38 = 64 g before and after.

items.q: What happens to atoms in a chemical reaction?
c: They are rearranged into new substances; none are created or destroyed.
items.e: This is the law of conservation of mass.

items.q:
Mass
an antacid tablet46 g
water14 g
total after reaction58 g
Mbali mixed an antacid tablet and water in an open cup. Gas bubbled out. Why is the total mass after the reaction 2 g less?
c: Atoms were destroyed in the reaction.
The gas escaped into the air, but the atoms were not destroyed.
items.e: In an open system, gas leaves the cup. In a sealed bag, the mass would stay the same.
